headline_marked: [[Apple's new Siri AI is 'one-dimensional']] compared to Google Gemini, beta users find
headline: Apple's new Siri AI is 'one-dimensional' compared to Google Gemini, beta users find
summary: While Siri offers improved world knowledge and excels in personal context with on-device processing, it functions as a 'one-dimensional chatbot' lacking Gemini's versatility and deep exploration modes.
details: Apple recently unveiled a much-improved Siri in the iOS 27 developer beta, a version built with Google's AI expertise. Despite this significant partnership, early impressions describe the new Siri as a "one-dimensional chatbot" when compared to Google Gemini.

Siri's world knowledge has significantly improved, now accurately answering general questions without needing to redirect to the web. However, its personality remains professional but flat, offering facts without deeper context or versatile exploration modes.

Google Gemini, in contrast, provides more naturally conversational responses, richer context, and multiple models, including a "Deep Research" mode. Siri AI does not allow users to choose or even see which of its four text-based models it is using, aligning with Apple's approach to simplicity.

During comparative tests, Siri rephrased information with clarity but made more mistakes than Gemini in current affairs and local knowledge. Gemini generally delivered more whimsical and detailed answers, while Siri's responses often read like a Wikipedia article, sometimes with an unrequested image.

Siri's primary advantage lies in its privacy and personal context capabilities, processing information on-device using a semantic index. This enables seamless integration with personal data from emails and calendars, an area where Gemini's cloud-based connections are less fluid or consistent.
caption:

headline_marked: [[Modded Steam Controller auto-charges]] itself like a robot vacuum via GitHub program
headline: Modded Steam Controller auto-charges itself like a robot vacuum via GitHub program
summary: An aerospace worker created a web app using computer vision and the controller's haptic motors to guide it back to its charging dock. No installation is needed, just a camera and a flat surface.
details: An aerospace worker and programmer developed a GitHub-hosted program that enables the Steam Controller to automatically move itself back to its charging puck. The web app, called the Auto-Charge Vision Tracker, uses a camera and computer vision to locate the controller and its dock.

Once positioned, the controller utilizes its powerful built-in haptic motors to creep towards the charging station when not in use. This innovative solution makes recharging more convenient, mimicking the autonomous behavior of a robot vacuum.

To use the web app, simply visit the website and connect your Steam Controller. You'll need a camera positioned directly overhead your desk to allow the computer vision to accurately track the controller and its charging puck.

While the app offers a unique use for the Steam Controller's haptic motors, it requires a flat surface free of obstructions for the controller to reach its dock. The constant vibration and movement can also cause abrasion on the controller's surface.

The creator, Ray Foss, suggests adding rubber feet to the controller to prevent wear and potentially improve its acceleration and handling. This modification highlights the versatility of the Steam Controller's design.

This project stands out from similar efforts by using computer vision for automated guidance, rather than manual control. It transforms the controller into a self-driving device, adding a layer of autonomy.

Despite some usability limitations, such as the controller's inability to navigate different surfaces, this project showcases Valve's commitment to user-driven innovation. Valve previously released CAD files for the Steam Controller and Puck, encouraging community modifications.
Enthusiasts can try this curiosity by visiting the Auto-Charge Vision Tracker website. The program's files are also available on GitHub for those who wish to explore and develop their own versions.
